chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said:

Hafs al-A'war asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was sitting with him, saying: 'There was a laborer for my father who worked at his mill, and he had some dirhams with us, and he had no heir.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'You give it to the poor.'

Then he said: 'What is your opinion regarding it?' Then he repeated the question to him, and he said to him the same thing. He repeated the question to him a third time, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'You seek an heir for him; if you find an heir for him, [give it to him], otherwise it is like your property.'
Then he said: 'What do you suppose you will do with it?' Then he said: 'You bequeath it; if a claimant comes for it, [give it to him], otherwise it is like your property.'

key_terms.كَسَبِيلِ مَالِكَ: Like your property / As your own wealth

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling for the money of a deceased person who has no heirs?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the methodological nuance of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), who uses iterative questioning to distinguish between the initial status of the funds as a trust (*amanah*) and their final disposition as inherited wealth (*mirath*). By confirming that the money becomes 'like your own wealth' (*kasabil malik*) upon the failure to find an heir, the Imam establishes the principle of *ghunm bil-ghurm* (profit follows liability), allowing the custodian to utilize the funds for personal benefit or bequest, a ruling deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding *bayt al-mal* and private property rights.
